note: Semaglutide CNS access mapping — fluorophore-conjugated tracing shows access to circumventricular and hypothalamic sites, not broad parenchyma.
Liraglutide reaches the arcuate nucleus and acts on POMC/CART neurons; access via accessible-from-circulation routes.
Vagal afferent and NTS contribution to GLP-1 / exendin-4 effects on food intake.
GLP-1R in the VTA and NAc; central exendin-4 reduces reward-driven food intake.
In-vivo fibre photometry: consummatory VTA dopamine reward signalling preserved or increased under semaglutide despite reduced appetite — complicates the simple blunting account.

Photometry-calibrated optogenetics: VTA dopamine neurons encode palatability and drive hedonic eating; semaglutide suppresses VTA-DA responsiveness during consumption, but palatable-food appetite and VTA-DA activity recover over repeated semaglutide dosing — adds a time-course axis to the dopamine-blunting question.

Systematic review of fMRI studies of GLP-1RA effects on brain responses to reward-related cues: 11 eligible studies (mostly food cues, one alcohol). Limited evidence tentatively suggests acute GLP-1RA may reduce food-cue reactivity in appetite and reward regions, but effects are inconsistent and may attenuate over time; most studies enrolled ≤20 participants per group. Preprint — not yet peer-reviewed.

Phase-2 randomised trial (n=48): low-dose semaglutide reduced laboratory alcohol self-administration, drinks per drinking day and craving; calendar drinks/day and number of drinking days were unchanged.
26-week randomised, placebo-controlled trial of semaglutide 2.4 mg in alcohol use disorder with comorbid obesity (n=108); significant reduction in heavy-drinking days versus placebo.
Semaglutide reduces alcohol intake; central amygdala GABAergic transmission implicated alongside dopaminergic effects.

Electronic-health-record cohort (n=83,825 with obesity): semaglutide associated with ~50–56% lower incidence and recurrence of alcohol use disorder versus other anti-obesity medications — observational, confounding-vulnerable.
EHR analysis of semaglutide and suicidal ideation: no increased risk; signal leans weakly protective.
Central GLP-1 engages stress / HPA circuitry; central amygdala involvement in aversive and anxiety-like responses.

Phase-3 EVOKE and EVOKE+ trials of oral semaglutide (up to 14 mg once daily) in early-stage symptomatic Alzheimer's disease; the primary cognitive endpoint (CDR-SB at week 104) was not met and both trials were discontinued. Topline reported December 2025; full results published 2026.
Review of preclinical GLP-1RA neuroprotection: BDNF, anti-inflammatory action, hippocampal plasticity in rodent and cellular models.

journal: Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol
note: Hindbrain GLP-1 / PPG neurons are suppressed in negative energy balance; ablation does not alter ad libitum chow intake.
Central PPG-NTS and peripheral GLP-1 systems suppress eating independently; vagal input to PPG neurons is not carried by GLP-1R afferents.
Chemogenetic activation of PPG-NTS neurons suppresses food intake; the neurons fire phasically to gastric distension.
Acute stress recruits hindbrain GLP-1 neurons; negative energy balance silences them, and central GLP-1R antagonism blocks stress-induced hypophagia.
Exendin-4 attenuates nicotine-induced locomotor stimulation, accumbal dopamine release, and conditioned place preference in mice.
The GLP-1 receptor agonist exendin-4 reduces acute and chronic cocaine self-administration and cocaine-induced striatal dopamine release in mice.
Liraglutide reduces heroin self-administration and drug-induced reinstatement of heroin-seeking in rats; cue-induced reinstatement was not reduced at the tested pretreatment interval.

Exendin-4 did not reduce morphine conditioned place preference, withdrawal, hyperlocomotion, or remifentanil self-administration in mice — reinforcement if anything increased — while the same agent did reduce alcohol self-administration. A negative control for the cross-reward thesis: GLP-1's anti-addiction effect does not appear to extend to opioids.
Case reports and clinician anecdote of reduced gambling, compulsive shopping, and nail-biting under GLP-1RA therapy — uncontrolled. (Project-curated aggregate entry.)
GLP-1 receptor mapping in the macaque brain — amygdalar GLP-1R expression substantially higher than in rodent surveys.
Head-to-head brain-uptake pharmacokinetics of 13 incretin-receptor agonists in mice — most cross the blood-brain barrier slowly and incompletely, with marked drug-to-drug differences in rate.
Once-weekly semaglutide reduced appetite, ad libitum energy intake and food cravings, and shifted food preferences away from high-fat foods, in adults with obesity.
Randomised placebo-controlled pilot trial: liraglutide slowed gastric emptying, increased satiation and reduced caloric intake in adults with obesity.
Dissociating the anorectic from the nausea-like effects of peripheral GLP-1 receptor agonists exendin-4 and liraglutide in rats — anorectic doses also produce pica and conditioned taste aversion.

Review of GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist neuroprotection in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease: downregulated brain insulin and growth-factor signalling and impaired energy utilisation as disease drivers, and their normalisation by incretin receptor agonists — the mechanistic basis of the 'type 3 diabetes' framing of Alzheimer's disease.

Electronic-health-record cohort analyses reporting lower dementia-diagnosis incidence under GLP-1RA prescription — the observational signal that motivated the EVOKE programme. (Project-curated aggregate entry; observational and confounding-vulnerable.)
